```{r read-data}
#| label: read-data

# prudence = "stingy" makes duckplyr stop with an error, instead of silently loading the
# whole table into R, when a verb can't run inside DuckDB. Reading, joining, filtering and
# summing below stay lazy; only small summaries are collected.
#
# Both branches below end with the same two tables, with lower-case column names: asv_counts
# (asv_id, sample, count; zero counts dropped) and asv_tax (asv_id, phylum, family, ...).
#
# ampliseq 3.0+ writes both as long tables in summary_tables/. Counts are DADA2's raw output,
# from before clustering and any filters, so ASVs that a filter removed have counts but no
# taxonomy row; they end up as `Unassigned` below. There is one taxonomy table per
# classifier and database (ampliseq.taxonomy.<CLASSIFIER>.<database>.parquet). This picks the
# consolidated DADA2 table if there is one, otherwise the first DADA2 table in alphabetical
# order; set tax_file by hand to use a different one. Check its header (`phylum` and
# `family` must be there).
if (file.exists("data/ampliseq.counts.parquet")) {
  asv_counts <- read_parquet_duckdb("data/ampliseq.counts.parquet", prudence = "stingy")

  tax_files <- Sys.glob("data/ampliseq.taxonomy.DADA2.*.parquet")
  tax_file  <- c(grep("consolidated", tax_files, value = TRUE), tax_files)[1]
  asv_tax   <- read_parquet_duckdb(tax_file, prudence = "stingy")
} else {
  # Before 3.0, ASV_table is wide (one column per sample). The UNPIVOT query reshapes it to
  # the long form inside DuckDB, without building the wide table in R, and drops zero counts.
  #
  # NOTE: verify the header of ASV_table.tsv against your actual file (`head -2
  # data/ASV_table.tsv`) before trusting this as-is -- the query assumes the first column is
  # named ASV_ID. Some ampliseq export paths prefix a leading "# ..." banner line before the
  # real header (QIIME/biom convention); if that's the case here, delete that line from the TSV
  # and re-run `make` in data/.
  asv_counts <- read_sql_duckdb(
    "SELECT ASV_ID AS asv_id, sample, count FROM (
       UNPIVOT read_parquet('data/ASV_table.parquet')
       ON COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE ASV_ID) INTO NAME sample VALUE count
     ) WHERE count > 0",
    prudence = "stingy"
  )

  # ASV_tax.<database>.parquet -- database name varies by run, hence the glob. Rank columns
  # are DADA2's own assignTaxonomy() output names, capitalized; renamed here to match 3.0.
  asv_tax <- read_parquet_duckdb(Sys.glob("data/ASV_tax.*.parquet")[1], prudence = "stingy") %>%
    select(asv_id = ASV_ID, phylum = Phylum, family = Family)
}

# Relative abundance is computed from the raw counts, per sample, *before* the taxonomy join
# -- this is what makes "keep the pre-removal relab for undefined taxa" work without extra
# bookkeeping: the denominator already includes every ASV, classified or not.
tbl <- asv_counts %>%
  mutate(relab = count / sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .by = sample) %>%
  left_join(asv_tax, by = "asv_id")

sample_metadata <- read_tsv("data/sample_table.tsv", col_types = cols(sample = col_character()))
```

# Results

## Taxonomic composition

```{r taxonomy-barplot}
#| label: fig-taxonomy-barplot
#| fig-cap: Phylum-level community composition, top taxa above 1% relative abundance; `Other` is below-threshold classified ASVs, `Unassigned` is ASVs with no phylum classification.

top_phyla <- top_taxa(tbl, phylum, relab, threshold = 0.01)
phylum_pal <- assign_palette(top_phyla, variable = "phylum")
barplot_tbl <- taxonomy_barplot_data(tbl, phylum, relab, top_phyla)

ggplot(barplot_tbl, aes(x = sample, y = value, fill = .display)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = phylum_pal, name = "Phylum") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative abundance") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
```

## NMDS

NMDS is rank-based and robust to the choice of transformation, so no transformation is
applied here -- Bray-Curtis dissimilarity on family-level relative abundance, with
undefined (unclassified) ASVs excluded before summing (not folded into an "Other" bucket,
unlike the barplot above). The distances come from `ecolongr::el_vegdist()`, which works
directly on the long table (one row per sample and taxon) without building the
samples-by-taxa matrix, and are then passed to `vegan::metaMDS()`.

```{r nmds}
#| label: fig-nmds
#| fig-cap: NMDS of family-level relative abundance (Bray-Curtis, no transformation).

d <- tbl %>%
  filter(!is.na(family)) %>%
  summarise(quant = sum(relab, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(sample, family)) %>%
  transmute(sample, taxon = family, quant) %>%
  el_vegdist("bray")

# trace = 0 silences the per-iteration console output; ord$tries hitting trymax (default
# 20) just means it used its full random-start budget, not that anything failed.
ord <- metaMDS(d, trace = 0)

scores_tbl <- as.data.frame(ord$points) %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
  left_join(sample_metadata, by = "sample")

treatment_pal <- assign_palette(sort(unique(sample_metadata$treatment)), variable = "treatment", palette = "Set1")

ggplot(scores_tbl, aes(x = MDS1, y = MDS2, colour = treatment, shape = site)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = treatment_pal) +
  labs(title = sprintf("NMDS, stress = %.3f", ord$stress))
```
